# `treeseg`: outline tree crowns {#sec-treeseg}

## What it does

`treeseg` divides a canopy height model into individual tree crowns. It
starts from each height peak and grows a region outward and downward
(a watershed segmentation) until neighbouring regions meet along the low
ground between crowns. Each crown gets an ID, an area, and a maximum
height, which support crown-size distributions, tree lists with crown
dimensions, and crown-level metrics.

`treeseg` finds its own peaks, so its crown count can differ from
`canopymaxima`'s tree-top count on the same canopy model.

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| (input) | `out/chm.tif` | The canopy height model from @sec-canopymodel. |
| `/output-raster` | `out/crown_segments.tif` | Raster of crown IDs. |
| `/output-table` | `out/crown_summary.csv` | One row per crown. |
| `/minht` | `2` | Cells lower than 2 ft belong to no crown. |

: Options used in the `treeseg` example. {#tbl-options-treeseg}

## Outputs

- **`crown_segments.tif`**: one band, `tree_segment_id`, holding each
  cell's crown ID (empty for cells in no crown).
- **`crown_summary.csv`**: one row per crown with `TreeID`, `MaxHeight`,
  `CrownArea` (in square units of the input, square feet here), and
  `PixelCount`.

## Results

@fig-treeseg-map draws the crown outlines (orange) over the canopy height
model, with the `canopymaxima` tree tops from @sec-canopymaxima (aqua)
for comparison. Outlines follow the visible crown edges and meet along
the low ground between crowns. Crowns with no aqua top inside show where
the two tools disagree. @fig-treeseg-sizes plots crown area against
crown height. Very small crowns at low heights are the most likely to be
fragments rather than trees.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/treeseg_figures.md >}}

## Checks

@tbl-checks-treeseg confirms that the table and the raster list the same
crowns, that each crown's pixel count and maximum height match the
raster and the canopy model, that crown area equals pixel count times
cell area, and that the area's unit label names the tile's own units.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/treeseg_checks.md >}}
